# Original LEZAC.EXE level-7 boss-head (GRAN.MST) per-tick motion evidence.
#
# Captured in-container: tools/seed_original_level.py drove the original from
# level 1 to level 7 through its own results routine (six natural
# transitions), then 775 consecutive game ticks were sampled tick-locked on
# the frame counter DS:0x78C2 with ONE 64 KiB pread of the whole data segment
# per tick, so no record can tear across the scattered tables.
#
# The head is actor slot 1 (kind 0x1e, behavior 6, visual 6); slots 2..7 are
# the six kind-0x1f segments (behavior 5) linked to it. Head position lives in
# the visual table DS:0xC21E (stride 8); the 8.8 fixed-point sub-pixel
# fractions and velocities live in the actor record: +0x06 vx, +0x08 vy,
# +0x0a x-fraction, +0x0c y-fraction.
#
# This also settles the DS:0x79EA question: the motion-link table is ONE-based,
# so slot 0's bytes are unrelated scalars -- byte 0 is the lives counter
# (observed 2 -> 1 when the boss reached the player) and byte 2 is the energy
# byte DS:0x79EC (observed 100). There is no lives/link-table collision.
#
# bottom= is DERIVED, not sampled: the original adds gravity 0x40 to vy only
# when the bottom collision flag is clear (file 0x673e: `cmp BYTE ss:[di-0x21],0`
# / `jne`), so a tick that did not take the +0x40 had the bottom flag set.
# The four edge flags themselves were not sampled.

boss_lockstep_original=level7
source=LEZAC.EXE via DOSBox /proc/mem runtime read
runtime_ds=0c8f
head_actor_slot=1
head_kind=0x1e
head_behavior=6
head_visual=6
head_box_width=5
head_box_height=4
segment_count=6
segment_kind=0x1f
segment_behavior=5
motion_link_index_base=1
motion_link_slot0_is_scalars=1
lives_offset=0x79ea
energy_offset=0x79ec
gravity_step=64
gravity_clamp=none
gravity_gate=bottom_flag_clear
reflect_rule=neg_half_trunc_toward_zero
rng_gate_modulus=29
rng_draw_order=roar100,speed800,jump1500
speed_base=150
speed_range=800
jump_base=300
jump_range=1500
roar_threshold=70
roar_cursor=0x0069
roar_priority=4
player_x=840
player_y=328
tick_count=775

# Orbit links (mode 0xff). Recomputed once per tick by 1000:432A BEFORE the
# actor loop, so their output uses the anchor's position from the PREVIOUS
# tick -- with that one-tick lag the output becomes a pure function of the
# phase byte (0 of 128 phases ambiguous; without it, all 128 are).
# The rule below is exact on 774/774 sampled transitions for every orbit link:
#   phase = (phase + gain) & 0x7f
#   out_x = anchor_x + off_x                            (no horizontal term)
#   out_y = anchor_y + off_y + trunc(sin[phase]*radius_y)
# radius_y is link byte +0x05; byte +0x04 is 1 for every orbit link and is NOT
# an x radius. orbit_phase_dy is the observed out_y - anchor_y curve indexed by
# phase 0..127.
orbit_anchor_lag_ticks=1
orbit_horizontal_term=none
orbit_rounding=trunc_toward_zero
orbit_table_scale=6.28
orbit_link 3 self_visual=5 gain=3 radius_y=7 byte4=1 off_x=-12 off_y=10 exact_x=774/774 exact_y=774/774
